subject.title: Browser: add explicit import from existing-session profile into managed openclaw profile

question: Should OpenClaw support explicitly copying signed-in existing-session browser state into a managed openclaw browser profile?
rationale: This crosses the browser isolation and sensitive-state boundary, so code can be written, but only maintainers can decide whether the product should support the import at all and what consent/safe-copy constraints are required.

options.title: Approve scoped import
options.body: Implement a one-shot local same-user import in the browser plugin with explicit consent, destination reset, transient-file filtering, source untouched, and docs/tests covering the security boundary.

options.title: Reject profile copying
options.body: Keep existing-session attach as the supported path for reusing logged-in state and document that managed openclaw profiles remain isolated from personal browser profiles.

options.title: Defer for security design
options.body: Keep this issue open but require a short design note covering browser artifacts, platform lock files, password-manager/sync state, and rollback before implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped import
recommendation.body: Implement a one-shot local same-user import in the browser plugin with explicit consent, destination reset, transient-file filtering, source untouched, and docs/tests covering the security boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across browser config, profile mutation, and docs ownership surfaces involved in this product/security boundary.
